# TRMNL plugin development

This is a workflow for private TRMNL plugins (HTML + Liquid + TRMNL framework classes) on the owner's TRMNL OG (og_plus, 800x480, 2-bit, 4 greys). It was worked out while building the owner's other webhook plugins.

**In this repository:** the markup lives in `trmnl/src/`, fixtures in `trmnl/fixtures/` (generated by `trmnl/tools/make_fixtures.py`), and `trmnl/tools/render.py` + `shot.mjs` + `sheet.py` implement the render / gate / contact-sheet loop below. See `trmnl/README.md`.

## Ground rules

- Show rendered views whenever you propose or change a screen, as a contact sheet of every affected view and mashup.
- Never send a layout for review before it passes the layout gate (check.py below), with every view and every state rendered.
- Never type the user's TRMNL API key anywhere: not into `trmnlp login`, a form or a config file. Uploads and previews go through the TRMNL connector (mcp__TRMNL__*). If an operation answers 403 (for example deleting a plugin setting), ask the user to do it.
- Ask before deleting anything of the user's (plugins, playlist items).
- Keep the data source dumb: push raw values, and put the logic (thresholds, mapping, wording) in the markup and in plugin custom fields.
- If a request is unclear, ask instead of guessing.

## Local workspace (in the scratchpad)

```
src/<plugin>/shared.liquid, full.liquid, half_vertical.liquid, half_horizontal.liquid, quadrant.liquid
data/<plugin>@<fixture>.json   merge variables for one state (add "__now": epoch to pin the clock)
data/<plugin>.fields.json      the plugin's custom field values (copy the live ones)
build/                         render.mjs, tl_render.rb, shot.py, check.py, diffbase.py, verify_upload.py, *.sh sets
ext/tl<ver>/lib                trmnl-liquid gem source
www34/css|js|fonts             framework assets for the version TRMNL serves
out/<set>/                     rendered pages and PNGs; out/baseline/ for pixel diffs
```

### Renderer: TRMNL's own Liquid, not a lookalike

TRMNL renders with the open-source `trmnl-liquid` gem (Ruby Liquid 5 plus TRMNL filters and the `template` tag). Use it so local output matches the server's.

- trmnlp (usetrmnl/trmnlp) needs Ruby 4 and wasn't usable here, and `gem install trmnl_preview` on Ruby 3.3 pulls an ancient 0.7.x. Instead, extract the gem: `gem fetch trmnl-liquid -v <ver>`, untar its `data.tar.gz` into `ext/tl<ver>`, then `gem install liquid redcarpet rqrcode tzinfo`.
- On Ruby < 3.4, replace the implicit block param `it` with `_1` in `lib/trmnl/liquid/filters.rb` (for example `def group_by(collection, key) = collection.group_by { _1[key] }`).
- `build/tl_render.rb`:
  ```ruby
  # encoding: utf-8
  require "json"
  require "trmnl/liquid"
  input = JSON.parse($stdin.read)
  env = TRMNL::Liquid.new
  print Liquid::Template.parse(input["src"], environment: env).render(input["ctx"])
  ```
  Call it as `ruby -E UTF-8 -W0 -I ext/tl<ver>/lib build/tl_render.rb` with `LANG=C.UTF-8`, passing `{src: shared + layout, ctx}` on stdin. Never use `ruby -e` with non-ASCII source.
- Build the context like the server does: merge variables at the top level, plus
  `trmnl: { user: { time_zone_iana: 'Europe/Warsaw', utc_offset: 3600, locale: 'en' }, device: { width: 800, height: 480, model: 'og_plus', bit_depth: 2 }, system: { timestamp_utc }, plugin_settings: { instance_name, custom_fields_values } }`.
- render.mjs wraps the output in the page skeleton: framework CSS + JS from www34, `<body class="environment trmnl">`, `<div class="screen screen--ogv2 screen--2bit screen--md screen--landscape screen--density-1x">`, then `mashup mashup--<layout>` (1Lx1R, 1Tx1B, 2x2, 1Lx2R, 2Tx1B, ...) containing `view view--<size>` divs. Usage: `node render.mjs out.html full home@fixture:full` or `node render.mjs out.html 1Lx2R home@x:half_vertical commute@y:quadrant today@z:quadrant`.
- Framework assets: `https://trmnl.com/css/<version>/plugins.css` and `https://trmnl.com/js/<version>/plugins.js`, plus the fonts the CSS references (TRMNL12/16/21, Inter, ...). Match the version the server uses. If the shell can't reach trmnl.com, ask the user to attach the files.

### Screenshots, gate, diffs

- `shot.py page.html ...`: Playwright Chromium at 800x480, scale 1, `--font-render-hinting=none --disable-font-subpixel-positioning`. It waits for `window.TRMNL_PLUGINS_READY === true`, then quantises to the 4 greys (0/85/170/255, no dithering) and writes page.png, page_raw.png and page_x2.png.
- `check.py page.html ...`: the layout gate. It must print `RESULT: PASS` and exit 0 before anything is shown or uploaded. It checks:
  1. The framework runtime finished.
  2. No view content overflows its cell (scrollHeight vs clientHeight, element rects inside the view).
  3. Chips are at whole-pixel positions and sizes.
  4. No chip text is clipped.
  5. Chip text is vertically centred: the gap above the capitals equals the gap below the baseline.
  6. Horizontal chip padding is equal within 2 px.
  7. No chips overlap.
  8. Chip text is at least 2 px from the inner edge.
  9. Chip baselines match neighbouring text on the same wrapped line. Skip siblings on other lines.
  10. No `Liquid error`, `{{`, `{%`, `undefined` or `NaN` appears in the page text.
  11. No icon has empty path data, and no image failed to load.
  12. No text or icon spills outside its tile or card.
  13. No value or title is truncated with an ellipsis.
- `diffbase.py`: pixel-diffs out/<set>/*.png against out/baseline/<set>_*.png. Snapshot a baseline before any refactor and expect `RESULT: identical`.
- Old-vs-new check for refactors: copy the deployed markup to `src/<plugin>old/` with the same fixtures, render both over many states (including empty data, no history, missing sensors, half the sensors `unavailable`) and diff the pairs. This found a 4 px spacing slip that the baseline didn't cover.
- Fixture matrix: for every view (full, half_vertical, half_horizontal, quadrant) inside the mashups the user actually runs, render calm, typical, several-problems, everything-wrong (stress), stale, empty and unavailable states. Then compose contact sheets and look at them.

## Framework facts (TRMNL framework 3.4.x, og_plus)

- View content boxes: full 780x410 (title bar 40 px), half_vertical 365x408, half_horizontal 760x173, quadrant 365x173. Budget heights as `408 - used` rather than 410 to avoid 1-2 px overflow.
- Fonts: `label` = TRMNL16 (16 px, line-height 20), `label--small` = TRMNL12.
- Value classes (Inter, size/line-height): xlarge 74/86, large 58/70, medium 38/42, small 26/29, xsmall 20/24.
- Greys: `bg--white`, `bg--gray-65`, `bg--gray-30`, ... They dither to 2-bit, so use flat greys only for fills and keep text black on white or white on black.
- Labels carry framework padding that throws chips off-centre on the device. Inside chips and pills, override it: `line-height: 14px !important; padding-top: 0 !important; padding-bottom: 0 !important;` (or 19 px for TRMNL16 in a 25 px chip with `padding: 1px 8px` and a 2 px border). Gate checks 5 and 8 catch regressions.
- Use MDI (Material Design Icons) path data in a JSON capture in the shared markup, parsed with `parse_json`. Inject only the icons used (mdi_inject.py, one per line) and re-run injection after removing an icon so no trailing comma breaks the JSON.

## Liquid on TRMNL: rules that bit

- Reusable components: `{% template name %}...{% endtemplate %}` in shared markup, used with `{% render "name", key: value %}`.
  - The closing tag must be written exactly `{% endtemplate %}`, without whitespace dashes, or TRMNL won't recognise it.
  - Templates have isolated scope, so pass everything they need (including the MDI hash).
  - No filters inside render arguments. Assign first, then pass the variable.
  - To return a number or several values from a template, `capture` its output and split it, for example `rows§row_rows§tiles§chips` with `split: "§"`, then `| plus: 0`.
- Inside `{% liquid %}`, comment with `#` lines. Comment blocks there are fragile.
- Arrays of objects: build JSON strings (`| json` to escape values), wrap them in `[...]`, `replace: ",]", "]"`, then `parse_json`. Sort with `sort: "rank"`. To sort strings numerically, zero-pad them (`value + 1000000`) and sort and reverse.
- Maths is Ruby: integer division truncates and floats leak decimals. Use `round`, and integer pixel maths everywhere (fractional sizes fail gate check 3).
- Time: `trmnl.system.timestamp_utc`, `trmnl.user.utc_offset`. For ISO times use `date: "%s" | plus: 0`. Day of week from epoch days: `(days) % 7` maps to Thu,Fri,Sat,Sun,Mon,Tue,Wed.
- Custom fields: `trmnl.plugin_settings.custom_fields_values.<key> | default: "x" | plus: 0`.
- The connector's markup linter warns about undefined variables inside templates and about inline styles. Both are expected and harmless.

## Layout principles the user signed off on (attention first)

- A fixed grid of equal tiles per view: full 4 across (up to 2 rows), half_vertical 2x2 (up to 3 rows), half_horizontal 4x1, quadrant 2 (2x2 when there are more problems). Never long or wide cards.
- Black tiles are problems, ordered by severity. White tiles fill the remaining slots by usefulness rank, so the slots are always used.
- One small row under the grid:
  - In a crisis, overflow problems appear only as black chips.
  - Otherwise, running devices appear as outline chips plus calm statuses (icon + text). Show calm statuses only if something more useful than outside temperature is among them.
  - Pack first fit using a glyph-class width estimate in tenths of a pixel (narrow ` il.:·'` 5 px, semi `jfr-1t` 7, wide `mwMWOGQC%` 15, otherwise 10; +22 px per chip, +31 px per calm item, 4 px gaps), with 46 px reserved for a "+N" chip. Nothing may be clipped.
- Never mix chips into charts or other ambient content.
- Ambient content (rooms, air, energy) fills whatever height is left: compute H, then choose type sizes, chart height and how many consumer rows fit.
- Overnight values: drop redundant words ("Sat 06:40" rather than "until Sat 06:40") when space is short.

## Deploy workflow

1. Render all sets, run check.py, take screenshots, and run diffbase or old-vs-new where relevant. Show the user contact sheets for any visual change.
2. Read every file to upload in full first. The connector takes content inline, so the exact text must be in context.
3. Upload with `AccountMarkupWriteTool` action `writeMarkup` (`plugin_setting_id`, `size` = markup_shared | markup_full | markup_half_vertical | markup_half_horizontal | markup_quadrant, `content`). Upload shared first, then the layouts, back to back.
4. Run `verify_upload.py`. It reads the session jsonl, takes the last writeMarkup content per plugin and size, and compares it with the local file. Hand-copying 50 KB is error-prone: it caught a `11.95` that became `11.950` in an icon path. Fix any mismatch, either by re-uploading or (only if it is provably harmless) by aligning the local file, and say so.
5. Run `startPreview` for each size with `device_model: "og_plus"`, then `getPreview` with the job id. Decode `preview_base64` from the session log by job-id regex rather than echoing it, compose a sheet (previews come back at half scale) and look at it. This is the proof that TRMNL's server accepts the markup with live data.
6. To test states without touching live data, use a copy plugin with static merge variables (webhook data gets overwritten by the collector). Ask the user to delete temporary copies afterwards if the connector can't.
7. Each render spends from the hourly render allowance (429 past it). Batch previews.
8. Report briefly: what changed, the preview sheet, and anything the user must do.
